facts.raw_span: A 61-year-old man presented with gross hematuria
Intravenous urography demonstrated a tubular filling defect with partial obstruction of the right mid ureter
Retrograde ureteropyelography confirmed a 5 cm long tubular mass in the mid ureter proximal to the iliac vessels
Urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy of the lesion and renal pelvis were negative for malignancy
A staging CT scan showed slight dilatation of the right renal pelvis and subtle thickening of the right ureter without evidence of metastasis or lymphadenopathy

concepts.why: The patient presented with gross hematuria and intermittent right pelvic pain, and imaging studies revealed a tubular filling defect with partial obstruction of the right mid ureter, which is consistent with a ureteral polyp.

aliases: Transitional cell carcinoma of the ureter

rationales.F09: Intravenous urography demonstrating a tubular filling defect with partial obstruction of the right mid ureter is highly suggestive of a ureteral polyp or carcinoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a pedunculated ureteral tumor with a vulnerable surface and negative urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy for malignancy supports the diagnosis of a ureteral polyp, while the lack of evidence for malignancy and the specific imaging findings make ureteral carcinoma a less likely but still possible diagnosis.
